features.description: Capture-time sanitization in the completion-audit evidence writer: workstation-specific paths and operator identity never reach disk.
features.acceptance: the envelope writer (the single function that persists audit-<auditor>-<i>.json and its transcript) sanitizes BEFORE writing: every absolute path under the operator's home directory in transcript_path, envelope_path, and raw_response is rewritten to a stable placeholder form (<home>-prefixed or repo-relative when the path is inside the repo), and the operator's username and user@host actor strings are replaced with <operator> / <operator>@<host> placeholders; sanitization happens in the WRITER so the in-memory transcript object returned to callers is the sanitized one (what the gate consumes equals what disk holds — no divergence); a written envelope re-read from disk parses with the existing envelope reader and the disposition parser unchanged; the transcript .txt sidecar receives the same sanitization; a regression test writes an envelope whose raw response and paths contain the real home directory and username (injected via the offline/dispatch seam, no paid call) and asserts the persisted bytes contain neither the home path nor the username while status/dispositions still parse; a no-op test asserts already-clean content passes through byte-identical; pure-function sanitizer is exported so the sufficiency (pre-impl) envelope writer can adopt it in a follow-up without re-implementation. all tests offline on temp dirs, zero paid calls.

features.description: Append-only re-audit: a completion re-audit writes the next iteration's envelope/transcript instead of overwriting the previous one.
features.acceptance: the iteration used by the completion-audit dispatch path is derived from the audit directory state: the next iteration is one greater than the highest existing audit-<auditor>-<n>.json for that auditor (1 when none exist); an explicit iteration argument passed by callers is honoured only when it does not collide with an existing envelope — on collision the writer refuses with an actionable error naming the existing file rather than overwriting (overwrite is impossible by construction, not by caller discipline); the envelope's recorded iteration field always equals the filename's <n>; the gate/close readers select the HIGHEST-iteration envelope for the auditor when consuming prior audit state; tests: two sequential audits via the injected dispatch seam produce audit-x-1.json and audit-x-2.json with the first byte-identical after the second run, the reader returns iteration 2's verdict, an explicit colliding iteration refuses with the named file, and mixed-auditor directories number independently per auditor. all tests offline on temp dirs, zero paid calls.
